rows.b: A compound semiconductor that moves electrons far faster than silicon, used in phone radios, lasers, and satellites. It costs more but wins where speed matters.
A crystal that switches power at extreme speed, shrinking phone chargers to pocket size. It also makes the blue and white LEDs that light the world.
A custom chip combining a strong processor and graphics to run detailed games on the television. It is tuned for one job: fast, beautiful play.
The very first transistors were built on germanium, which switches at lower voltage than silicon. It ruled the early years before silicon took over.
A server packed with graphics processors that do thousands of simple calculations at once. It trains AI models and renders films in hours instead of months.
A sheet of carbon one atom thick that conducts electricity better than copper and is stronger than steel. Transistors built on it could switch at extreme speeds.
